correctness.rationale: Finite-dimensional trace-norm duality gives a common contraction for each pair precisely when two polar graph supports are orthogonal. The graph bases are globally orthogonal, with input and output coordinate-projection energies each exactly one-half per rank vector, so Bessel forces sum rank <=2min(p,q). Signed coordinate matrix units attain this; square extremal rank rigidity follows from m=2d and all ranks>=1. Star embedding equivalence follows by translating the center. Fourier and rectangular numeric checks are supplementary.

value.rationale: The natural matrix trace-class extremal packing problem has a sharp rank-weighted obstruction that survives all noncommutative directions; it determines the smallest matrix size for every unit star, and it rigidly classifies all cardinality-maximal square examples via balanced unitary frames. This replaces a diagonal construction with a genuine universal noncommutative theorem; no external downstream theorem is assumed.
